channel.title: RSS Aggregator Feed
channel.description: An aggregated feed of Technology-related news

item.title: Ukraine's next weapon against Russian drones is this slightly odd tiny robot which fires nets into the air in all directions
item.description: Ukraine's VORON ground robot uses net launchers to intercept FPV drones while supporting logistics, evacuation, reconnaissance, and other frontline missions.

item.title: Trump’s DOJ gains oversight of OpenAI’s green-card employee sponsorships
item.description: The DOJ alleged that OpenAI did not meaningful attempt to hire U.S. citizens before seeking permanent residence for Visa-holding employees.

item.title: Meta enters the AI coding wars with Muse Spark 1.2 and Muse Code with persistent async background agents
item.description: Meta today released Muse Code, a terminal-based AI coding agent now in beta, alongside Muse Spark 1.2, a coding-focused update to its Muse Spark family of frontier models — a one-two punch that puts the company in direct competition with Anthropic's Claude Code, OpenAI's Codex, and the growing field of agentic coding harnesses that have rapidly become the primary way many professional developers ship software."Releasing Muse Code in beta today," Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg wrote in a post on rival social network X (under his longtime handle @finkd). "It's a terminal coding agent that takes on com...

item.title: Engadget Indie Pitch: 'VILE: Exhumed' physical edition
item.description: "Play an interactive video nasty."

item.title: The National Design Studio Became a DOGE Landing Pad. Now ‘Big Balls’ Is Recruiting
item.description: WIRED spoke with an engineer who was interviewed by Edward “Big Balls” Coristine for a government engineering role at the NDS, the White House agency staffed by other DOGE veterans.

item.title: Moove raises $250M to become the backbone of the robotaxi industry
item.description: Moove is scaling up the autonomous vehicle fleet management side of its business and plans to someday own, not just manage, Waymo robotaxis.

item.title: How Lightspeed found its newest hire … via Instagram DM
item.description: Lightspeed partners Josh Machiz and Claire Zau stopped by the Equity studio to talk about the strategies behind their growing social media presence and their podcast, Lightwork.

item.title: Why Lightspeed is going all-in on creator-led venture capital
item.description: Venture firms are turning to creators to build trust with the next generation of founders before a check is ever written. It’s a trend that’s been building with a16z’s acquisition of Erik Torenberg’s Turpentine podcast and OpenAI’s acquisition of TBPN. Lightspeed Venture Partners just made its own notable hire in that vein, bringing on Claire Zau, a seed investor with a major following on Instagram and […]...

item.title: DHS Wants Protesters’ Signal Group Chats
item.description: A lawsuit accuses Homeland Security of violating protesters’ free-speech rights—but the agency is using it to try to get access to the plaintiffs’ encrypted communications.

item.title: Disney's latest TikTok deal shows it's betting on real creators instead of AI-generated videos
item.description: Disney is bringing creator-made vertical videos to Disney+ through a new partnership with TikTok, giving select creators access to its iconic franchises. Beyond the new content, the deal signals a broader shift toward embracing authentic fan creators over AI-generated videos.

item.title: Tech giants struggle to censor graphic videos of Perez Hilton appearing to harm himself
item.description: The disturbing livestream originally appeared on TikTok and quickly spread. Users and experts alike say social networks need better moderation systems. Major social media platforms are once again under fire for their flawed approach to content moderation after a disturbing livestream from Perez Hilton, in which the celebrity blogger appeared to be committing acts of self harm, flooded into people’s news feeds....

item.title: Senate advances the latest Kids Online Safety Act out of committee
item.description: The House passed its own version of the contentious KOSA bill in June.

item.title: Klaviyo acquires Elias Torres’ Agency in full-circle reunion for tech founders
item.description: The serial entrepreneur joins the e-commerce company as CPO to lead its AI agents.

item.title: South Korean military signs deal to turn flying taxis into troop transports — and the US Air Force could be next in line
item.description: South Korea will adapt Archer's Midnight flying taxi for military missions while supporting certification work and future commercial air mobility development.

item.title: E.l.f. Beauty acquired Rhode for $1 billion a year ago. It’s been a great investment so far
item.description: The CEO of Rhode tells us about the beauty brand’s plans to go international and how it’s balancing a thriving DTC business with physical retail. Today the beauty conglomerate E.l.f. Beauty released its earnings, delivering growth of 36% in net sales, to $479.4 million, across its portfolio of brands.

item.title: Demis Hassabis steps down as DeepMind CEO, plus more Google leadership changes
item.description: Hassabis will take on a new role as Google DeepMind chair and Alphabet’s chief scientist. Major leadership changes were announced at Google Wednesday.

item.title: Someone stole every Flock camera in this Minnesota city
item.description: A city lost its entire Flock camera network as communities nationwide grapple with the controversial license plate readers.

item.title: Elon Musk: 'At some point, Starlink will deliver a majority of the world's internet,' but that promise hinges on launching thousands more next-gen satellites and the massive Starship working as promised
item.description: Starlink head Elon Musk believes he can serve most of the world's Internet in less than a decade, but is that claim realistic?

item.title: The Most Dangerous AI Hacking Techniques Still Have Humans in the Loop
item.description: Security researcher James Kettle tried to push the limit of AI’s hacking abilities—and discovered how effective it can be when combined with human expertise.

item.title: TikTok Says ‘Moderator Error’ Kept Perez Hilton Livestream Up
item.description: The gossip blogger was on TikTok covered in what appeared to be blood and wielding a knifelike object before the platform cut his stream. He’s since been hospitalized.

item.title: Jeff Dean and other top AI researchers are leaving Google to launch their own startup
item.description: The legendary Google executive is joined by other outgoing Google execs in a joint mission to use AI to push forward the process of scientific discovery.

item.title: A prestigious university used AI to monitor its entrance exam. It turned into a disaster
item.description: Protestors are rallying as experts estimate up to 75,000 test-takers may have cheated on the exam for Mexico’s largest university. Last week, protestors rallied outside the largest university in Mexico, chanting, “We demand honesty, not artificial intelligence.” The National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM) had moved its highly competitive entrance exam online for the first time ever, complete with an AI proctor—and now it seems under that proctor’s not-so-watchful eye, tens of thousands of applicants are suspected to have cheated....
